model_interpretation.claim: Computing two targets per thread should reuse each source particle's position and mass across both interaction calculations, reducing source-load instructions per output. The explicit 128-thread/256-target mapping preserves coalesced target groups and guards partial groups. The extra accumulators and reduced thread-level parallelism may instead increase register pressure or lower occupancy; measurements across scored sizes are needed.

items.subject: Per-thread target coarsening without shared memory
items.objective: Explore per-thread register coarsening only: each thread computes multiple distinct target particles while reusing source values in registers. Do not use shared-memory source tiling or block-level multi-output assignment, so this contrasts with T1. Set block and items_per_block to implement an explicit, unique target mapping (for example, items_per_block as a multiple of block); handle partial groups and write each output exactly once. Measure the reuse, register-pressure, and parallelism tradeoffs across all scored sizes under the official protocol, after full correctness checks.
